title: The Rise of the Ottomans
objective: After this level you can describe how the Ottoman Empire grew.
summary: Founded by Osman I about 1300, the Ottomans crossed into Europe as Byzantine allies and took Gallipoli in 1354. Nearly destroyed by Timur in 1402, they reunited by 1413 and lasted until 1922.

cards.headline: Around 1300, the Ottomans were a small band in Anatolia. They lasted 600+ years.
cards.body: Level 87 showed them taking Constantinople. How did a chief’s followers get that far, and why did they nearly not make it?

cards.headline: Osman’s people, invited in
cards.body: The name comes from the founder: Osman I, a Turkmen chief who founded the dynasty and the empire about 1300, near Bursa in Anatolia. His son Orhan’s big break came from the Byzantines themselves. He crossed into the Balkans as the ally of a future emperor, John VI, and married his daughter Theodora. In 1354 the Ottomans took Gallipoli as a permanent foothold in Europe. Some guests never leave.

cards.headline: An army that never went home
cards.body: From the late 14th century the sultans built an elite corps, the Janissaries. They were recruited by taking Christian boys from the Balkans and converting them to Islam. They are called the first modern standing army in Europe: soldiers kept permanently ready, not called up for one campaign.

cards.headline: Nearly the end, in 1402
cards.body: Then a bigger conqueror arrived. In 1402 Timur, from Central Asia, crushed Sultan Bayezid I near Ankara, and Bayezid died in captivity. Timur split the Ottoman lands among Bayezid’s sons, who fought each other until Mehmed I reunited them in 1413. Forty years later, Mehmed II took Constantinople. Knocked down, not knocked out.

cards.context: At its height it reached the gates of Vienna. From a frontier band around 1300, it lasted more than 600 years, long after the Middle Ages had ended.

cards.headline: The Ottomans: understood
learned: Osman I founded the dynasty about 1300
They took Gallipoli in 1354 as a foothold in Europe
Timur nearly broke them in 1402; they reunited by 1413

questions.prompt: Where does the name “Ottoman” come from?

options.label: The town of Bursa
options.rationale: Bursa was near where they began.

options.label: A Byzantine emperor’s daughter
options.rationale: Orhan married Theodora; the name is Osman’s.

questions.explanation: Ottoman is a dynastic name from Osman I, who founded the dynasty and empire about 1300.

questions.prompt: Why was 1402 nearly the end of the Ottoman state?

options.label: Constantinople’s army drove them out of Europe
Timur crushed Bayezid I and split his lands among his sons
The Black Death killed the whole army
options.rationale: That was decades earlier, and it wasn’t the cause.

questions.explanation: Timur defeated Bayezid I near Ankara and divided Ottoman lands; civil war followed until 1413.

questions.prompt: The Ottomans gained a foothold in Europe at Gallipoli in 1354. Where did Mehmed II move his capital in 1453?

options.label: To Bursa
options.rationale: That was near where Osman began.

options.label: To Edirne
options.rationale: He moved his capital away from Edirne.

options.label: To Ankara
options.rationale: That’s where Bayezid lost to Timur.

questions.explanation: After the conquest, Mehmed moved his capital from Edirne to Constantinople.
